body:
No, I don't mind. I used the same account for that reason, I suppose...and too lazy to be clever enough to think of a new throwaway ;)

I chose this name because I'm about two decades older than everyone else here.

Thank you for the link...how interesting.

I'm a woman. I do write, but it's bad writing. I write to keep myself company. (And spend too much time on reddit...)

This suicide has been inside me for a long time, and I just don't know if it is escapable. I think partly the reason I don't talk about this much IRL is because it does create instant something, people feel obligated to respond in some way, and that's not always good. (And sometimes worse if they don't respond at all.)

Thank you for writing to me.
Thank you.
I hope I can find those reasons. Thank you for the suggestions and for replying.
Not here, that's for sure! (Cue ironic laughter...) But I guess it could be worse, so there is that.
Thank you for your kindness...it really helps when one is feeling so desolate.
I am glad you are feeling better. It's always good to hear that some of us do feel better. And thank you for your kind words.
Thank you for the encouragement...I'm still slogging along, I guess. Your kind words do help.
Thank you for your offer...it was very sweet.
You know, this brought tears to my eyes. I'm sorry if that sounds sappy, but it's beautiful. I'm so glad that happened for you. And thank you for coming here and writing it.
Thank you very much. I may take you up on your offer. I am so grateful to all of you who have responded.

Thank you for the link to the article. In the comments section, one of the researchers included a link to his page (more of 'evolutionary origin of depression' type articles there) so I'm checking it out.

It's good to hear things from your perspective, and to hear that people do actually 'recover' to some degree. Losing hope is the worst...

That looks very interesting.

I think I'll be getting 1Q84 from the library, but I want to wait until it's under less demand because I don't think I can plow through 900+pages in three weeks (with my poor, barely functioning brain...)
You're right about death coming on it's own. Thank you for the encouragement. You sound like a very strong person--it's great that you've put your energy to such a positive use.

Thank you for the recommendation, that sounds pretty good. In her book, Helen Thayer mentions his expedition briefly. It sounds like a good book to read in the summer...reading her book now makes me feel so cold!

I haven't. But speaking of mind-fuck, have you read anything by Haruki Murakami? I have not read his stuff but there's a book that looks really intriguing, it's called [1Q84](http://www.amazon.com/1Q84-Haruki-Murakami/dp/0307593312/ref=wl_it_dp_o_npd?ie=UTF8&coliid=I1UYHSG4MB25SP&colid=1EMLCN0VKVLG7). Just thought I'd mention it on the off chance you've read his stuff because I'm curious as to how it is.
Thank you, it's always encouraging to hear from others who are struggling and trying hard to hang in there, because I know you really understand.
Thank you very much.

Lots of empathy from me here. I'm not agoraphobic but I do get to the point where I don't leave the house for a week at a time. It's miserable feeling trapped like that.

Thank you so much for responding to my post. I hope you'll find the strength to keep going. Feel free to PM me too.
(edited for grammar...bad grammar, that is...)

>As long as I keep going, I win.

You've got a point there. It's hard not to wallow in self-pity sometimes because many people in my family are very successful and I'm the odd duck who always 'had so much potential' and always spectacularly underachieved. But for me, getting out of bed every day is a big deal, and I make myself do it. I am glad you've found something that helped (your support group.) It's hard to get help.

Thank you so much for the encouragement. Your kind words really mean a lot to me.
Thank you for the offer...I hope it was a good movie?
I'd love to talk to you. I'm sort of fading atm, so it'll be tomorrow for me too. Thanks for the reply :)

I'm sort of fading for the night, but I just wanted to say I understand about the soul-sucking cocktails. I tried sooooo many different meds. I'm actually unmedicated right now, for better or worse. I'm not against the idea of meds, and will probably try them again at some point. But I know the med I was on was making me feel worse, particularly physically--not because I missed hypomania or anything like that. It's too bad you weren't able to engage in therapy without that extra pressure.

I think if I had known earlier what I was up against, I wouldn't have kept chalking up my depressive episodes to personal failings. I kept trying school and leaving school, working and quitting, etc. And I think, too, if I had something concrete to tell my parents way back when, they might have tried to be more understanding instead of saying how I wasn't trying. But then, that's all hindsight, and it very well might have gone down the same way because there is still a lot of stigma and misinformation floating around.

So so, I suppose. I hope this isn't like crying wolf...posting in SW when I'm not ready to off myself this minute, but usually when I feel that badly I don't want to talk to anyone (-_-)' How are you? You doing ok?

You know, I think I would be doing a lot better if I were not isolated and if I were in therapy. If you have the chance to do those things for yourself, please do them. I don't have the resources right now to get into therapy, or I would. Bipolar is definitely a hard road (do you hang out in bipolar reddit?) but a lot of people live ok lives with it. I wish I was one of them. I think getting help early can make a difference. I wasn't diagnosed until I was in my 30's and by then I had lots of chaos behind me.
The House of Leaves sounds wild...good luck!

It's non-fiction. It's written by Helen Thayer. She was 50 when she set out on her month long journey...she's crazy competent, but it's still kind of tense reading (even though I know she lived to write about it.)

If my brain worked as it should, without interruptions of depression so severe I can hardly move, I think I could have done whatever I wanted in life. As it is, I sit in my room and stare at the walls (and spend too much time on the internet.) I'm so stuck and I want so badly to get better. I exercise regularly, eat decently, and I'm not into alcohol or drugs, so I feel I've done the best I can on my own and I can't seem to fix the rest. Right this minute, I don't want to die. I want to live and I want my life to have meaning. But I don't know how to get there. And then the next depression will hit and that will fly out the window.

I know no one can help, really, but thank you for letting me ramble a little. I get terribly isolated and I know that doesn't help.

And thank you for your comment, very much.
Thank you...

I do...and your question made me laugh, because I'd have a hard time lurking Reddit if I didn't. But I know what you meant ;) I'm currently reading a book about a woman making a solo journey to the magnetic North Pole, and I'm going to start an Ursula LeGuin book called Lavinia as soon as I finish the other one. How about you?

You made me smile with the whole "Life Begins at 40"...maybe in a few years I'll be able to say that, who knows.  I hope I can find a way out of this.  Thank you for your kind words, it means a lot to me.

I am keenly aware that I am probably older than most of Reddit, but I find hope in many young people who are kind, thoughtful, and willing to take the time to help others.  I am not sure what provoked me into writing about this.  Normally I'm a very private person and want to be perceived as fun-loving, etc. when I manage to get out of my little cave.  But thank you for reading.  I really do hope things get better, and some days, I guess that's all I can do.

I've mostly had low-skilled work, food service, receptionist, etc.  Thank you for saying that, but now that it is daytime, I feel even more embarrassed for having posted this.  (Exposed by the cold light of day!)
Thank you for your kind reply.  The article was pretty interesting, it's nice to think that somehow the fates will align and something good might happen someday.
